title.narrative: Provision of Integrated Life-Saving Assistance to Vulnerable Communities in Baydhaba District to Address Drought Impacts and Prevent Displacement.

description.narrative: ltpgtHRDO (HIDIG Relief and Development Organization) is proposing a 12-month integrated, multi-sectoral project in Baydhaba, one of the flagship districts under the Standard Allocation (SA2 2025) Strategy – Flagship Initiative. The project will deliver life-saving assistance to the most vulnerable communities, addressing the worsening impacts of drought and reducing displacement risks. Baydhaba, one of 32 districts reprioritized under the HNRP 2025, hosts the second-largest IDP caseload in Somalia and contains pockets of acute vulnerability, particularly in rural areas with limited humanitarian access. Without timely intervention, households will face increased displacement toward urban centers, creating further displacement cycles and additional strain on overstretched service delivery hubs. lt/pgtltpgtThe project will target underserved rural populations with urgent humanitarian needs, prevent avoidable displacement through area-based, origin-focused interventions, and strengthen community engagement and collaboration with government actors to ensure equitable and accountable distribution of resources. The integrated multi-sectoral approach will be essential to address the complex and interrelated needs of communities, combining interventions across nutrition, health, WASH, protection, and livelihoods to maximize life-saving impact and resilience. Guided by the Flagship Initiative strategy, this proposed project will implement activities based on the recommendations of the Baydhaba Area-Based Coordination (ABC) following initial community consultations conducted in the first phase of the allocation strategy. This approach has ensure that crisis-affected communities in the target villages remain at the center of the response. Programming will be anchored in community-defined priorities to maximize relevance and impact, reframing assistance from the ground up. By integrating multiple sectors, the project will respond holistically to immediate humanitarian needs while addressing underlying vulnerabilities, enabling communities to recover, strengthen resilience, and reduce reliance on repeated emergency interventions.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtProtection will be fully mainstreamed throughout the project cycle. HRDO will ensure the inclusive participation of women, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups, while mitigating risks of abuse, exploitation (including SEA), GBV, and neglect. Inclusive access will be promoted through mobile services, equitable information dissemination, targeted advocacy, and vulnerability-based targeting with reinforced safeguards. HRDO will build local capacity, strengthen referral systems, and coordinate with GBV actors identified in Baydhaba to support survivors of abuse and displacement. Robust coordination and reporting mechanisms will underpin the project, with HRDO leading monitoring alongside ABC structures and OCHA’s Field Coordination Unit (FCU). Monitoring and evaluation tools will be from relevant clusters and line ministries, with digital reporting/tools applied where feasible. Activities will include joint field visits, quarterly progress reviews, and after-action learning reviews, ensuring adaptive programming aligned with national cluster systems and ministry frameworks to reinforce accountability, transparency, and quality across all components.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtHRDO has worked in Baydhaba for the past 12 years, accumulating extensive knowledge and experience in implementing humanitarian and development projects across the district. This long-term presence has established strong trust and acceptance within communities, enabling HRDO to engage effectively with local leaders, women, youth, and marginalized groups. The organization’s familiarity with local dynamics, social networks, and service gaps will ensure that interventions are contextually appropriate, widely accepted, and responsive to the needs and priorities of the most vulnerable populations.lt/pgt
